ENV-01.sheet: A single 3D-model reference turnaround sheet on a plain light-gray studio background: the same floating shelf of dark rock 40 m wide and 56 m long with a ragged asymmetric outline, about 6 m thick at the rim and tapering into an inverted cone 48 m deep with a faint bronze vein glowing inside it, six thick rusted chains hanging from bronze rim rings into the haze. At the near end is the SPAWN TERRACE, an irregular paved patch about 13 x 9 m of cracked slabs of different sizes, with a shallow bronze arrival disc (3.6 m across, three concentric rings, slightly sunken and cracked) at its centre and a low broken rock lip behind it; a tiny plain 1.8 m human silhouette stands on the disc facing the door in every view for scale. A broken road of uneven worn slabs about 4 m wide, with a thin broken bronze inlay line, leads about 11 m to THE BEAM: one colossal weathered bronze I-girder 16 m long with a 2.5 m wide top, lying slightly crooked (about 15 degrees off the straight line) across a ragged meandering crack that cuts the whole island from rim to rim, 8 to 11 m wide with stepped broken lips and a 60 m drop into haze; the beam is level but dented, rust-streaked, matte, dusty, with missing rivets and a chipped corner, never polished. Beyond it a broken irregular forecourt about 13 x 4 m, then three worn uneven steps rising to THE DOOR, shown LOCKED, cut into the face of a huge black rock cliff with raw rock on both sides: 8 m high, carved stone frame 7.6 m wide with a crown of bronze finials, battered green-bronze verdigris scrollwork leaves dark with soot, two thick rusted chains wound across both leaves held by one huge closed padlock, a thin bright amber line of light through the centre gap, exactly like the Core Fantasy key-art door. Behind the door the cliff holds a walkable antechamber: a 3 m passage, then an irregular carved hall about 16 x 11.5 m with an 11 m cracked ceiling, four stout columns (two whole, two broken) around a clear aisle, a low round dais 4.5 m across where three weapons hover, one shaft of amber light through a ceiling hole, a small west alcove, and a 4 m exit tunnel in the east wall opening onto a rock ledge on the cliffs east face where a fixed bridge leaves toward the next island. A very tall ruined carved tower (60 m, irregular broken tiers, sheared top, a few dim amber windows, no domes) and a shorter leaning half-collapsed tower (36 m) grow out of the cliff above the hall, with six jagged black rock spires of 20 to 48 m between and around them. Three bare dead trees (6 m, 4.5 m, and a 2.8 m broken stump) stand off the road, a few small uneven clumps of dry grass, and rubble in uneven scatters of different-sized stones; no mirror symmetry anywhere, immense, silent and ominous; match the attached approved ENV-01 hero image and blueprint sheets exactly, and add no second floating island or extra rock in the background, shown from 6 angles in one image, arranged in a clean grid (front, back, left side, right side, top, underside). Every view must be the exact same object with identical design, proportions and scale, rendered with neutral even studio lighting and no shadows hiding detail, no scene, no camera tilt. A large bold title banner at the top reading exactly "ENV-01 - STARTING SHELF ISLAND" with a smaller size note "~40 x 56 m" beside it, and a small label under each view with the angle name; all text short, high-contrast, spelled correctly, each label appears only once. Every island must have a dramatically unique, instantly recognizable grand silhouette with one signature feature, immense sense of scale, mysterious ancient engineered ruins, deep volumetric haze and warm rim light, interesting to look at from every angle. Match the approved key art: weathered sandstone-tan and dark charcoal-brown layered rock with obsidian-black shards, warm gold-amber dusty haze light, photoreal cinematic game-asset concept, rough eroded surfaces with sharp fractured edges, sparse dry dead fossil-like trees and thin dry grass tufts only. REAL, NOT A TOY: photoreal massive geology and ancient ruined architecture, as if photographed at full size. Heavy erosion, soot, dust, deep cracks, spalled and chipped stone, rust and verdigris streaks, irregular asymmetric forms. NOT a toy, NOT a miniature or diorama or snow-globe, NOT smooth clay or plastic, NO tidy repeating wedding-cake tiers, NO cute rounded domes, no cartoon proportions, no flat even colour. Matte grimy materials, one low warm sun, deep shadows, strong rim light. NATURAL, NOT STAGED: nothing stands alone like a prop on a table; every structure is grown out of, carved into or half-buried in the rock, bases merged with scree, rubble and fallen blocks. Irregular organic outlines, uneven ground, off-centre and overlapping forms, no neat rows, no mirror symmetry, one obvious focal point. Ruins, NOT a city, no skyscrapers, no glass, no modern architecture, no green lush vegetation.
